prompt_text: Who is the best moving company in Pleasanton CA for a local move?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single universally “best” mover — the right company depends on your needs (size of move, how much packing/insurance you want, budget, move date, stairs/elevator, parking constraints). I can help you find the best fit. To get you started, here’s a quick plan and what to look for when choosing a local mover in Pleasanton, CA.

What matters most
- Proper licensing: For moves inside California, confirm the mover has a California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) household goods carrier number.  
- Insurance and valuation options: Ask about basic liability vs. full replacement value and any deductible.  
- Experience with local moves and any specialty items (pianos, gun safes, antiques).  
- Clear pricing: binding estimate or binding not-to-exceed vs. verbal lowball quotes.  
- Reputation: Google and Yelp reviews, recent customer photos/comments, and BBB rating.  
- Availability and responsiveness on phone/email.

How to pick the best company (step-by-step)
1. Get 3 on-site (or video) estimates — not just phone quotes.  
2. Compare written estimates line-by-line: hourly vs flat, packing, fuel, travel time, extra fees (stairs, long carry, bulky items).  
3. Ask about crew size and estimated hours, equipment (truck size, blankets, dollies), and COVID/policy changes.  
4. Check references or recent reviews mentioning similar moves to yours.  
5. Confirm the contract: move date/time, cancellation policy, insurance/valuation, payment methods (avoid large cash deposits).

Red flags
- Demanding large upfront cash deposits.  
- Only giving vague or significantly lower verbal quotes, then “adjusting” the price up on moving day.  
- Poor communication, many unanswered questions.  
- No written estimate or license number when asked.

Typical questions to ask a mover
- Are you licensed by the CPUC? What’s your carrier number?  
- Do you provide binding or non-binding estimates?  
- What valuation/insurance options do you offer?  
- What is included in the price (packing, supplies, disassembly/reassembly)?  
- How many movers and what truck size will you send?

If you want, I can:
- Narrow the list to 3–5 well-rated local movers near Pleasanton (I’ll need permission to search current listings and reviews).  
- Draft an email or script you can use to request quotes.  
- Help estimate cost if you tell me: move date, pickup and delivery ZIP codes, number of bedrooms, any large/heavy items, stairs/elevator, and whether you need packing.

Tell me which of the above you’d like me to do next (or provide move details) and I’ll proceed.
